bull.b: Multi-year revenue expansion demonstrates sustained commercial traction in prostate diagnostics and indicates a growing installed base and clinician adoption. That scale supports operating leverage potential, deeper payer engagement, and a larger addressable market for cross-selling, underpinning durable top-line growth prospects.

Sustained ~60% gross margins reflect strong unit economics for the core tests, providing a structural buffer for profitability as volumes grow. High product-level margins enable investment in sales and R&D while improving the odds that scale will translate into durable operating leverage and eventual positive free cash flow.

Completed sales-force integration and AI/clinical initiatives create a stronger, more efficient commercial model and differentiated evidence base. Building an AI data platform and embedding AI endpoints in trials can raise clinical value, support payor coverage, and provide a sustainable competitive moat over the medium term.

bear.b: Negative equity and materially higher debt levels signal a weakened capital structure, increasing refinancing and dilution risk. This constrains financial flexibility, may raise funding costs or force dilutive financings, and limits the company's ability to absorb shocks or invest opportunistically over the next several quarters.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow indicate the business still requires external funding to sustain operations and integration costs. Until cash generation turns positive, the company faces runway and liquidity constraints that could force financing decisions that materially affect long-term capital structure and strategic optionality.

Exiting the Resolve business reduces revenue diversification and signals payer uncertainty; a potential $10.4M recoupment creates contingent liability and a protracted appeals process. Both factors weaken reimbursement credibility, add restructuring costs, and heighten execution risk in payer negotiations over the medium term.
